Definition: probably from a primary ἕπω (to be busy about); an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war):--armour, instrument, weapon.
BiblicalUsage: I take hóplon to mean armour, instrument, weapon, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 5 times, and John and Romans show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: hóplon matters to me because the weapons of our warfare are not carnal — they are mighty through God. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
RelatedEvents: The Arrest of Jesus in Gethsemane
